rules.title: Statewide prohibition on local rent control (M.G.L. c. 40P § 4)
rules.requirement: No Massachusetts city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind. The only exception is a city or town that accepts the chapter. It may adopt rent control only if compliance becomes voluntary after six months, the rules do not cover evictions, occupancy, services or condo conversion, they exclude owners of fewer than ten units and units with fair market rent over $400, and the municipality pays owners the difference from fair market rent.

exemption_conditions.condition: Permitted rent control regulation may not apply to any rental unit owned by a person or entity owning less than ten rental units
Permitted rent control regulation may not apply to any rental unit with a fair market rent exceeding $400

coverage.notes: The prohibition applies to all cities and towns. The exception applies only to municipalities that accept chapter 40P. In those municipalities, owners' compliance becomes voluntary after six months from initial adoption, and the municipality must pay owners the difference between fair market rent and controlled rent from its general funds. The ten-unit threshold counts all rental units the owner holds, not units per building.

rules.coverage_text: The rule applies to every city and town in Massachusetts and bars local rent control. A municipality that accepts chapter 40P may adopt only voluntary, compensated rent control. That regulation cannot cover units owned by someone with fewer than ten rental units, or units with a fair market rent over $400.
rules.exemptions: Permitted local rent control may not apply to units owned by a person or entity owning less than ten rental units, or to units with a fair market rent exceeding $400. After six months, owners may decline to participate, and their property is wholly unaffected.
rules.interaction: State law preempts local rent control: no city or town may enact, maintain or enforce it except under the limited conditions in this section. Any permitted local regulation may not regulate occupancy, services, evictions, condominium conversion or the removal of properties from regulation.
citation_aliases: General Law - Part I, Title VII, Chapter 40P, Section 4

llm.notes: The document is M.G.L. c. 40P § 4, the state ban on local rent control, so I recorded it under rent_increase_limits as a state preemption rule with no specific cap value. The ban on local regulation of evictions in subsection (b) is described in interaction rather than recorded as a separate just-cause rule. The text gives no enactment or effective dates.
